title: Frigidaire vs. Honeywell Dehumidifier (2026): Which to Buy?
dek: Both remove a genuine 50 pints a day — as long as you buy the right Honeywell. Here's how they compare, and which Honeywell "50" to skip.
description: Frigidaire vs. Honeywell dehumidifier: the FHDD5034Y1 and TPFIT50PWK compared on real DOE capacity, coverage, drainage, warranty and recall history.
intro: The Frigidaire vs. Honeywell dehumidifier matchup is mostly a naming puzzle. Both brands sell a model that removes a genuine 50 pints a day under today's test, and both back their compressors with five years of sealed-system coverage. But they suit different basements — Frigidaire's adds Wi-Fi and voice control, Honeywell's adds a built-in pump — and the two come from very different supply chains.

The biggest trap is Honeywell's naming. Frigidaire's **FHDD5034Y1** is rated at a genuine 50 pints a day under the current 2019 DOE test. Honeywell's true equivalent is the **TPFIT50PWK**, a newer TP-Fit model rated at 50 pints with a built-in pump. But not every Honeywell that says "50" delivers it: the TPFIT50AWK, which Consumer Reports scored an 88, and the Wi-Fi TP50AWKNR are both rated at only about 32 pints a day under today's test, so neither is a like-for-like rival.
We compared the two using DOE ratings, manufacturer specs and warranty terms, published independent scores and the CPSC recall database. We don't run our own lab tests.
topPicksLead: For most shoppers, the **Frigidaire FHDD5034Y1** is the better buy for its larger rated coverage, Wi-Fi with Alexa and Google, and low-temperature defrost; the **Honeywell TPFIT50PWK** matches its 50-pint capacity and is the one to pick if the unit sits below your nearest drain and needs a pump.

products.whyWeLoveIt: This is the Honeywell that genuinely matches the Frigidaire on capacity: a 50-pint, ENERGY STAR model from Honeywell's newer TP-Fit series. Where the Frigidaire relies on a bucket or a gravity hose, this one adds a built-in pump, so it can run unattended in a basement that sits below the nearest drain.
products.performance: Honeywell rates it at 50 pints a day for spaces up to 4,000 square feet. The pump handles drainage when gravity can't, laundry mode speeds drying for clothes hung indoors, and auto-comfort mode picks a humidity target for you. Thermal overload protection guards the compressor. There's no app, so if remote control matters more than a pump, the Frigidaire is the better fit. head: Frigidaire FHDD5034Y1
Honeywell TPFIT50PWK
blocks.caption: Ratings from manufacturer specs and listings; warranty terms are each brand's published coverage.

blocks.text: We matched each brand's closest current genuine 50-pint model and compared them on capacity under the 2019 DOE procedure, manufacturer spec sheets for coverage, drainage and low-temperature operation, and published warranty terms. We added independent scores where they exist, checked the CPSC recall database for both brand names and read owner reviews for patterns around reliability and service. We do not lab-test dehumidifiers.

sections.heading: The naming gap: why a Honeywell "50" isn't always 50 pints

blocks.text: In 2019, the Department of Energy lowered its dehumidifier test temperature from 80°F to 65°F. Cooler air gives up less water, so every unit's rating dropped by roughly 30%. Frigidaire renamed its models to match the new figures. Honeywell's names are a mix: some still carry the old pre-2019 number, while its newer pump model's "50" matches today's rating.

items: **Honeywell TPFIT50AWK:** "50" in the name, about 32 pints under today's test — not a true match.
**Honeywell TP50AWKNR:** a Wi-Fi model once labeled 50 pints, now rated 32 under today's test — not a true match either.
**Honeywell TPFIT50PWK:** "50" in the name, 50 pints with a built-in pump — the true match for the Frigidaire.
**Frigidaire FHDD5034Y1:** "50" in the name, 50 pints under today's test.

blocks.title: Shopping tip
blocks.text: Ignore the number in any model name and look for the DOE 2019 rating on the spec sheet or EnergyGuide label. Our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) explains how much capacity your space needs.

sections.heading: Who makes them, and their recall histories

blocks.text: Neither brand builds its own dehumidifiers. Frigidaire's current units come from a licensed manufacturer in Midea's family, the same group behind several other brands we cover. Honeywell's are made by JMATEK, which has operated as Honeywell Air Comfort since 2014 — an entirely separate supply chain.

Both names appear in old fire-hazard recalls, but from unrelated manufacturers. Frigidaire was one of 13 brands on a Gree-built platform recalled in 2013 and reannounced in 2016 after roughly 450 fires. Honeywell-branded units built by New Widetech (models DH45W, DH50W and DH70W) were among about 20 brands recalled in 2021 after more than 100 overheating and fire incidents. Neither recall covers the current models compared here, but always check a secondhand unit's model number and date code at CPSC.gov.

For most homes, the **Frigidaire FHDD5034Y1** is the smarter purchase: a genuine 50-pint dehumidifier with the larger rated coverage, Wi-Fi with Alexa and Google, and auto-defrost to 41°F. The **Honeywell TPFIT50PWK** removes the same 50 pints a day and is the one to pick if you need a built-in pump — just skip the TPFIT50AWK, whose "50" label hides a 32-pint rating. Whichever brand you lean toward, compare dehumidifiers on their DOE 2019 rating, never on the number in the model name.

faqs.q: Is Frigidaire or Honeywell the better dehumidifier brand?
faqs.a: For most homes, Frigidaire, by a narrow margin. Its FHDD5034Y1 and Honeywell's TPFIT50PWK both remove 50 pints a day, but the Frigidaire has the larger rated coverage, Wi-Fi with Google Assistant and Alexa, and a published low-temperature rating. The Honeywell wins if you need a pump. Just don't confuse it with the TPFIT50AWK, which has a strong Consumer Reports score (88) but is rated at only about 32 pints a day.

faqs.q: Is the Honeywell TPFIT50AWK really a 50-pint dehumidifier?
faqs.a: No. Its name references the pre-2019 rating scale. Under the current DOE test it's rated at roughly 32 pints a day. Honeywell's genuine 50-pint model compared here is the TPFIT50PWK, which adds a built-in pump.

faqs.q: Are Frigidaire and Honeywell dehumidifiers made by the same company?
faqs.a: No. Frigidaire's current dehumidifiers are built under license by a Midea-family manufacturer, while Honeywell's are made by JMATEK, operating as Honeywell Air Comfort. They share no hardware platform.

They're close: Frigidaire offers one year on parts and labor plus five years on the sealed refrigeration system, and Honeywell's dehumidifiers carry a five-year limited sealed-system warranty. Some reviewers report that Honeywell's out-of-warranty repairs can be slow and costly.

faqs.q: Have Frigidaire or Honeywell dehumidifiers been recalled?
faqs.a: Both brand names appear in older recalls from different manufacturers: Frigidaire in the Gree recall first announced in 2013, and Honeywell-branded New Widetech units in a 2021 recall. Neither affects the current models compared here. Check any used unit at CPSC.gov.
